metadata.title: feat: Add OpenTelemetry W3C Baggage support for distributed tracing
metadata.author: vishu-bh

description:
## 🔗 Related Issue
Closes #3976

---

## 📝 Summary

This PR implements **OpenTelemetry W3C Baggage support** for distributed tracing context propagation in the MCP Gateway. It adds the ability to extract HTTP headers and convert them to W3C baggage, enabling rich contextual metadata (tenant IDs, user IDs, correlation IDs) to flow through distributed traces.

**Key features:**
- **Secure header-to-baggage conversion** with strict allowlist validation (fail-closed security model)
- **BaggageMiddleware** for automatic extraction from incoming requests
- **W3C baggage propagation** to downstream services (opt-in via configuration)
- **Enhanced OTEL tracing** with request-root spans for transport endpoints
- **Plugin execution tracing** with detailed span attributes for observability
- **Security controls**: value sanitization, size limits, DoS prevention, audit logging

**Architecture:**
- Dual processing model: strict validation for headers, permissive for existing baggage
- Configuration-driven with JSON-based header mappings
- Integration with OpenTelemetry context API for automatic span attribute injection
- Graceful degradation when OpenTelemetry is not available

## 📓 Notes

**Configuration Example:**
```json
{
  "OTEL_BAGGAGE_ENABLED": true,
  "OTEL_BAGGAGE_HEADER_MAPPINGS": [
    {"header_name": "X-Tenant-ID", "baggage_key": "tenant.id"},
    {"header_name": "X-User-ID", "baggage_key": "user.id"}
  ],
  "OTEL_BAGGAGE_PROPAGATE_TO_EXTERNAL": false
}
```

**Security Considerations:**
- Baggage propagation to external services is **disabled by default** (security-first)
- All header values are sanitized (CRLF removal, control character stripping)
- Size limits prevent DoS attacks (max 32 items, 8KB total by default)
- Only explicitly configured headers are processed (fail-closed model)
- Sensitive query parameters (session_id, sessionid) are redacted from trace spans

**Testing Coverage:**
- Unit tests: `test_baggage.py` (447 lines, 100% coverage)
- Integration tests: `test_baggage_middleware.py` (351 lines)
- E2E tests: `test_baggage_tracing.py` (232 lines)
- Security tests: `test_baggage_security.py` (389 lines)
- Observability tests: Enhanced `test_observability.py` (+569 lines)

**Performance Impact:**
- Minimal overhead when disabled (single boolean check)
- O(1) header lookups via pre-built hash map
- Lazy configuration loading on first request
- Non-pooled MCP sessions now emit detailed client lifecycle spans

**Breaking Changes:**
- None - feature is opt-in via configuration
- Default behavior unchanged (baggage disabled)

**Related Files:**

- Config: `mcpgateway/config.py` (+46 lines)

- Main: `mcpgateway/main.py` (+22 lines)

commits.message:
feat: implement OpenTelemetry baggage header extraction (GitHub #3976)

Implements HTTP header-to-baggage conversion for distributed tracing with strict security controls:

**Core Features:**
- Dual trust model: UNTRUSTED headers (strict allowlist) vs TRUSTED baggage (permissive)
- Size limits (32 items, 8KB) apply ONLY to header-derived baggage
- Default behavior: capture as span attributes only
- Downstream propagation requires explicit opt-in via config flag

**Implementation:**
- mcpgateway/baggage.py: Core validation, parsing, and conversion logic
- mcpgateway/middleware/baggage_middleware.py: ASGI middleware for extraction
- mcpgateway/config.py: 7 new configuration fields with Pydantic validation
- mcpgateway/main.py: Middleware registration after OpenTelemetryRequestMiddleware
- mcpgateway/observability.py: Auto-inject baggage as span attributes, conditional propagation

**Security:**
- Reuses existing sanitize_header_value() and ALLOWED_HEADERS_REGEX
- Strict allowlist (only configured headers processed)
- CRLF injection prevention
- Size limits enforced (DoS prevention)
- Audit logging for rejected headers
- Fail-closed on errors

**Configuration:**
- OTEL_BAGGAGE_ENABLED: Enable/disable feature (default: false)
- OTEL_BAGGAGE_HEADER_MAPPINGS: JSON array of header-to-baggage mappings
- OTEL_BAGGAGE_PROPAGATE_TO_EXTERNAL: Enable downstream propagation (default: false)
- OTEL_BAGGAGE_MAX_ITEMS: Max items from headers (default: 32)
- OTEL_BAGGAGE_MAX_SIZE_BYTES: Max total size (default: 8192)
- OTEL_BAGGAGE_LOG_REJECTED: Log rejected headers (default: true)
- OTEL_BAGGAGE_LOG_SANITIZATION: Log sanitization events (default: true)

**Testing:**
- 44 unit tests (baggage.py logic)
- 13 integration tests (middleware flow)
- 6 E2E tests (full tracing flow)
- 18 security tests (deny-path scenarios)

Closes #3976

Signed-off-by: Bob Shell <bob@contextforge.ai>
Signed-off-by: Vishu Bhatnagar <vishu.bhatnagar@ibm.com>

commits.message:
fix: correct middleware order and inject baggage into request spans

- Swap BaggageMiddleware and OpenTelemetryRequestMiddleware registration order
  (ASGI executes in reverse, so baggage must be set before span creation)
- Add baggage injection to OpenTelemetryRequestMiddleware request spans
- Update FastTimeUser load test to include baggage test headers
- Add baggage configuration documentation to .env.example

This ensures baggage attributes appear in all spans, including the root
request span created by OpenTelemetryRequestMiddleware.
